outcome: No human-verified resolution of the GNRS conjecture was found as of 11 October 2026. The one new development that bears directly on it is an OpenAI repository release, first public on 6 October 2026, whose manuscripts claim (a) a single constant for ℓ1 distortion of all planar graphs and (b) a constant C(k) for graphs of bounded treewidth. Both are attributed in the repository to an unreleased internal OpenAI model, both Lean main theorems are proved by sorry in the copies I read, and neither has a named human author or any public expert verification. Partial progress in the same window: Chang, Conroy, Eliot, Le and Vinayak (arXiv 2610.10888, 7 October 2026) give poly(k) ℓ1 distortion for k-outerplanar graphs, improving 2^O(k).
problem_asks: Read as the bullet states it, with 'minor-closed' taken as 'proper minor-closed'. The family of all graphs is minor-closed and has unbounded distortion, so the bullet cannot mean it; Wikipedia and ProofAtlas both say 'other than the family of all graphs'. Parts: (1) For each proper minor-closed family F of finite graphs, a real constant c(F) such that every connected finite graph G in F, with arbitrary positive edge lengths, has its shortest-path metric embed into an L1 (ℓ1) space with distortion at most c(F). (2) The constant depends only on F, not on the number of vertices of G or on its edge lengths; this uniformity is what makes 'bounded' non-trivial. (3) The question is asked for all proper minor-closed families at once, so a yes answer needs every such family, and a result for some families is a case, not the whole question. Not asked by the bullet but part of the literature's statement: the converse (a family has bounded distortion only if it excludes some minor), and the equivalent flow form (the multicommodity max-flow/min-cut gap is bounded on each such family, since c1(G) equals the flow-cut gap of G).

events.what_happened: OpenAI's openai/math repository, first public commit 6 Oct 2026 ('Initial commit'), contains a manuscript titled 'Planar Graph Metrics Embed into L1 with Constant Distortion'. Its folder is labelled 'Planar-Graph-Metrics-Embed-into-L1-with-Constant-Distortion-September-23-2026'; that date is a label inside the repository, not a recorded public posting date. The repository lists it as an accompanying paper of lean/ComparatorChallenges/PlanarL1.lean (the Lean docs file lean/docs/089.md names both papers). My tools could not extract the PDF's text, so the content is known only from the Lean statement, the Lean docs, the repository README, and a reader's blog (minorfree.github.io/OpenAIDump, entries 7 to 11 Oct 2026). I found no arXiv, journal, or referee posting of it, and no human author is named in what I could read.
events.revisions: Repository commit 3014888 on 8 Oct 2026, 'Update manuscripts and Lean formalizations'. The commit page does not show whether the planar folder or PlanarL1.lean changed. The folder label reads September-23-2026.
events.delivers: Per the Lean MainStatement in PlanarL1.lean: one real constant C of at least 1, the same for all graphs, such that every finite connected planar graph on Fin n with symmetric positive edge lengths admits a map f from its vertices into an L1 space (Lp Ω ℝ 1 with an arbitrary measure) satisfying graphDistance(x,y) ≤ ‖f x − f y‖ ≤ C · graphDistance(x,y). That covers all planar graphs with no restriction on size or edge-length ratios. Only the planar family is claimed. The Lean file gives no numerical value for C. The manuscript's own text was not read.
events.remains: Every other proper minor-closed family, that is, every proper minor-closed family not contained in the planar graphs. The general GNRS statement is not addressed. Lee and Sidiropoulos's reduction, as cited in the search summaries (full text not opened), puts the general conjecture into the planar conjecture plus a k-sum embedding conjecture, and the manuscript as read does not address k-sums. The reader's blog says the minor-free case is 'not included among Open AI solution'.

checked_by.who: Hung Le (author of the 'Rambling on Graphs' blog, minorfree.github.io)
checked_by.qualification: Co-author of the 2026 k-outerplanar ℓ1 paper (arXiv 2610.10888) and of the 2024 planar-to-bounded-treewidth embedding paper (arXiv 2411.00216). The blog says he and Arnold Filtser have studied these two problems for over a decade.
checked_by.what_they_did: Read the manuscript from 7 to 11 Oct 2026, by his own account for about 3 to 6 hours a day. Says the lemmas in the first 12 pages are 'straightforward'; calls Section 3 'only 4 pages long, but full of gibberish'; reports the proof introduces a 'non-crossing column model' he had not seen before; reads the statement of Theorem 4.1 and skips its proof; says 'the details are not in Section 5'; says the writing is 'so compressed and dense' and that the expanded version he produced with an AI assistant runs to 90+ pages. Gives no verdict on correctness, and on 11 Oct says he is still reading.

events.time_since_posted: 5 days as of 11 Oct 2026. The only public reading I found is the reader's partial one above; I found no reply from Filtser, Gupta, Newman, Rabinovich, Sinclair, Lee, Sidiropoulos or Naor.

machine_checked.note: 51-line file, read at repository main on 11 Oct 2026 through a fetch tool, not built locally. The statement MainStatement is written out in full. The main theorem planar_graph_metrics_embed_L1 : MainStatement is proved by sorry (line 47), so the file formalizes the statement but does not prove it. events.doubts: (1) In the copy read, the Lean main theorem is proved by sorry, so the formalization is not a machine check of the claim. (2) The repository's own README warns that 'Some of the unformalized results could have issues', and about 42% of top-line results are formalized according to its summary. (3) The reader's reactions (blog, 7 to 11 Oct): the proof rests on a model and a 'chart' that the reader found hard to follow, Section 3 'full of gibberish', Theorem 4.1's proof skipped, Sections 5 and 6 unclear to the reader. These are one partial reader's impressions, not a refutation. (4) No named human author, no arXiv or journal record and no referee report. (5) The same batch saw three manuscripts withdrawn one day after release for a sign error and fourteen revised with proof repairs, according to secondary summaries; per those summaries none of the withdrawn items is on ℓ1 embeddings, and the revision status of this manuscript is unknown.
events.direction: Affirmative for the planar family. It asserts that planar graphs have bounded ℓ1 distortion, which is the direction the conjecture predicts for that family. It says nothing about the other proper minor-closed families.
events.object: No counterexample. The object is an embedding: for each planar graph with positive edge lengths, a map of its vertices into an L1 space with distortion at most one universal constant C. The Lean statement is existential (there exist C, a measure space, and f), so the construction is not visible in the statement. The reader describes the argument as built on a 'non-crossing column model' and a 'chart'. Whether the construction is explicit or non-constructive was not established from what I read.

systems.name: an unreleased internal OpenAI model
systems.what_it_did: According to the repository README, the 'vast majority of results' in the batch were obtained with one procedure using this model. The README names two exceptions, a zero-free-region result for the Riemann zeta function and a proof of the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties; this planar manuscript is not among them. Humans grouped the outputs into families and applied a significance threshold, and the README describes human editing only for a readability edit to one zeta writeup. The repository text attributes the mathematics to the model, but I could not read the manuscript's own account of how it was produced, so the attribution here is the repository's.

A manuscript titled 'L1 Embeddings of Graphs of Bounded Treewidth' (folder label 'L1-Embeddings-of-Graphs-of-Bounded-Treewidth-September-23-2026') is listed as the companion of the planar manuscript, with lean/ComparatorChallenges/BoundedTreewidthL1.lean as its formalization. The reader's blog lists it with an 'Open AI solution' link and gives no reading of it. A third-party catalogue (sites.pitt.edu, not opened; search snippet only) describes it as resolving the bounded-treewidth case positively. The PDF text was not extracted by my tools.
events.revisions: Same as the planar event: repository commit 3014888 on 8 Oct 2026; the commit page does not show which folders changed.
events.delivers: Per the Lean MainStatement in BoundedTreewidthL1.lean: for every k of at least 2 there is a constant C of at least 1 such that every connected finite simple graph with a tree decomposition of the stated bag-size parameter k, with arbitrary positive edge lengths, admits an ℓ1 embedding of its shortest-path metric with distortion at most C. The constant depends on k, which the statement allows. Each bounded-treewidth minor-closed family is thereby covered, with one constant per k. I did not check the file's definition of the tree-decomposition predicate, so whether the parameter is the bag size or the width is not confirmed.
events.remains: Every proper minor-closed family without bounded treewidth, and the general GNRS statement. Bounded-treewidth families contain all trees, so the Lee–Sidiropoulos result for families that do not contain all trees (arXiv 0910.1409, opened) does not cover them. Per the sources, treewidth 2 was known (Chakrabarti et al. 2008), so the treewidth k at least 3 case would be new if this manuscript is correct. The Lee–Sidiropoulos k-sum reduction also still applies to the general case.

events.what_happened: arXiv 2610.10888, 'Peeling Half the Onion: Embedding k-Outerplanar Graphs into ℓ1 and Trees with a Polynomial Distortion (in k)', by Hsien-Chih Chang, Jonathan Conroy, William Eliot, Hung Le and Vinayak. Submitted 7 Oct 2026, cs.DS with cs.CG cross-listing, marked as a SODA'27 submission. The method removes k/2 layers per step, giving embeddings of k-outerplanar graphs into trees and into ℓ1 with distortion poly(k). The abstract states the previous best bound was 2^O(k), from Chekuri et al. (SODA 2003).
events.revisions: v1 only, per the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: For the family of k-outerplanar graphs, for each fixed k: ℓ1 distortion poly(k), improving 2^O(k). The family already had a constant depending on k from Chekuri et al. What moves is the dependence on k, which the GNRS statement does not ask for. Restricted to k-outerplanar graphs. A search snippet of the full text, not the abstract I opened, says O(1) distortion for planar graphs follows when k is constant; that is a restricted planar case.
events.remains: All other proper minor-closed families, the general GNRS statement, and planar graphs of unbounded outerplanarity depth. The abstract calls the planar ℓ1-embedding conjecture 'still-open'.
events.doubts: No active doubt raised. The 'still-open' sentence was most likely written before the 6 Oct repository release, since the paper is a SODA'27 submission, so it is not a rebuttal of the OpenAI planar claim. One of the authors, Hung Le, is also the reader who wrote the critical blog about the OpenAI manuscript; that is a relationship for the judging pass to note, not a doubt about this paper.
events.direction: Partial and in the affirmative direction for k-outerplanar graphs: it improves the constant's dependence on k without changing the GNRS question for that family.
events.object: A construction, not an object: for each k-outerplanar graph, an embedding into a tree metric or ℓ1 with distortion poly(k), via onion peeling that removes k/2 layers per step. The abstract does not say whether the construction is explicit beyond its method.

events.what_happened: arXiv 2411.00216, 'Embedding Planar Graphs into Graphs of Treewidth O(log³ n)', by Chang, Cohen-Addad, Conroy, Le, M. Pilipczuk and P. Pilipczuk, submitted 31 Oct 2024. It gives a stochastic embedding of planar graphs into bounded-treewidth hosts with treewidth O(ε⁻¹ log³ n).
events.revisions: v1 only, per the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: A stochastic embedding into bounded-treewidth graph hosts, not into ℓ1. It does not bear on the ℓ1 distortion question the GNRS conjecture asks.
events.remains: The whole GNRS question, which concerns ℓ1 distortion.
events.direction: Not in the direction of the ℓ1 question. A different embedding target.

The abstract states that every K_r-minor-free graph embeds into ℓ∞ with distortion O(r) in dimension Õ(r²)·log n.
events.delivers: ℓ∞ embeddings of K_r-minor-free graphs with distortion O(r). No ℓ1 statement in the abstract.
events.remains: The GNRS question, which concerns ℓ1.
events.time_since_posted: about 2 years 8 months as of 11 Oct 2026.
events.direction: Not an ℓ1 result. Discarded as a different target (ℓ∞), though the topic is adjacent.

events.what_happened: arXiv 2507.06576, 'Improved Lower Bounds on Multiflow-Multicut Gaps', by Sina Kalantarzadeh and Nikhil Kumar. v1 9 Jul 2025, v2 5 Oct 2025, v3 7 Oct 2025; a preliminary version appeared at APPROX-RANDOM 2025. The paper shows the multiflow–multicut gap is at least 16/7 for planar graphs, improving a lower bound of 2.
events.delivers: A lower bound of 16/7 on the multiflow–multicut gap (minimum multicut against maximum multiflow) for planar graphs. Per the paper's own definition this is a related but different gap, not the multicommodity flow–cut gap or ℓ1 distortion that the GNRS question concerns. The abstract page does not mention GNRS or ℓ1.
events.remains: Not applicable: it does not address the GNRS quantity.
events.direction: Lower bound on a different planar gap. Discarded as a neighbouring question, though the Filtser 'Fil+24' bounded-treewidth multiflow–multicut result cited in this paper is a lead I did not identify.

The abstract cites Kawarabayashi and Sidiropoulos's O(log² n)-approximation for multicut in planar digraphs, which also bounds the multicommodity flow–cut gap of planar digraphs, against an Ω̃(n^{1/7}) lower bound for general digraphs due to Chuzhoy and Khanna.
events.revisions: v1 only, per the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: Directed planar graphs. Not undirected ℓ1 embeddings, so not the GNRS quantity. Discarded as a directed analogue.
events.remains: Not applicable.
events.direction: Not in the direction of the undirected GNRS question. A directed-graph result.

events.remains: Not applicable.

events.what_happened: Gupta, Newman, Rabinovich and Sinclair, 'Cuts, trees and ℓ1-embeddings of graphs', Combinatorica 24 (2004) 233–269, with a preliminary version at FOCS 1999. Per Wikipedia and secondary citations, this paper formulates the conjecture (the search summaries and ProofAtlas both date it to 2004) and gives constant-distortion ℓ1 embeddings for series-parallel graphs and for graphs of bounded circuit rank, with an Ω(log n) lower bound for series-parallel graphs into distributions over dominating-tree metrics. I did not open the paper itself, so which version first states the conjecture is not confirmed.
events.delivers: Constant ℓ1 distortion for series-parallel graphs and bounded-circuit-rank graphs (restricted classes). The conjecture is posed for minor-closed families. Its flow–cut equivalence is recorded in the same line of work.
events.remains: The general conjecture.

events.what_happened: Chekuri, Gupta, Newman, Rabinovich and Sinclair, 'Embedding k-outerplanar graphs into ℓ1', SODA 2003; SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics 20(1), 2006, pp. 119–136 (the journal details come from a search result). It shows that k-outerplanar graphs, for fixed k, have constant-distortion ℓ1 embeddings, via distributions over tree metrics. The 2^O(k) dependence is attributed to it by the 2026 Chang et al. abstract, which I opened. The paper itself was not opened.

events.remains: All other proper minor-closed families, and the general conjecture.

checked_by.qualification: Peer review at a journal of record and at a conference

events.what_happened: S. Rao, SoCG 1999: every n-vertex planar graph embeds into ℓ1 with distortion O(√log n). This remains the best known upper bound for planar graphs. The bound is confirmed by an opened source (Filtser's 2019 abstract, which states it as the best known upper bound), and by Wikipedia. The 1999 paper itself was not opened.
events.delivers: ℓ1 distortion O(√log n) for every n-vertex planar graph. Not constant; the planar case of the conjecture is open with this bound.
events.remains: The planar conjecture (constant distortion), and therefore the general conjecture.

checked_by.where: Not located; cited by Wikipedia's GNRS article (opened) and by Filtser's 2019 abstract (opened)

events.direction: Partial: an O(√log n) bound, which is unbounded in n and so does not settle boundedness for planar graphs.

events.what_happened: James R. Lee and Anastasios Sidiropoulos, 'On the geometry of graphs with a forbidden minor', STOC 2009 (per a search result), and the arXiv paper 'Pathwidth, trees, and random embeddings' (arXiv 0910.1409, first submitted 8 Oct 2009). The arXiv abstract, which I opened, states that every shortest-path metric on a pathwidth-k graph embeds into a distribution over trees with distortion c(k), and that 'the preceding embedding theorem is used to prove this conjecture whenever the family F does not contain all trees'. Per search summaries of the STOC paper (not opened), it also reduces the GNRS ℓ1 conjecture to a planar conjecture and a k-sum embedding conjecture.
events.delivers: Settles the GNRS conjecture, in the affirmative, for proper minor-closed families that do not contain all trees, that is, families that exclude some tree as a minor. Those families have bounded pathwidth. It does not settle families containing all trees, which includes the planar family and every bounded-treewidth family of width at least 2.
events.remains: Families that contain all trees, including the planar graphs and bounded-treewidth families of width at least 2, and the general statement, which the search summaries say reduces to a planar conjecture and a k-sum conjecture.

checked_by.qualification: Peer review at a refereed conference

events.direction: Affirmative for families that do not contain all trees. Reduces the rest of the problem to the planar and k-sum statements, per the search summaries.

events.what_happened: James R. Lee and Daniel E. Poore, 'On the 2-sum embedding conjecture', SoCG 2013. Per the abstract on Lee's publication page (opened), the paper 'prove[s] the conjecture holds for any finite family of graphs F', where the conjecture is the Lee–Sidiropoulos 2-sum embedding conjecture, and it gives an O(log n) distortion bound for path metrics on 2-sums of copies of K_n. Wikipedia lists the 2-clique-sum case as a known bounded-distortion result citing this paper.
events.delivers: Claims the 2-sum (k = 2) embedding conjecture for every finite family F. The 2-sum conjecture is one of the two pieces the Lee–Sidiropoulos reduction names for the general GNRS statement, so the claim would remove the k = 2 piece if correct. It addresses k = 2 only; the planar conjecture is separate.
events.remains: The planar conjecture, and any k-sum statement for k of at least 3 that the abstract does not address. The status of k = 2 is disputed (see disputes).

checked_by.qualification: Peer review at a refereed conference
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper for SoCG 2013 (per the author's publication list)

events.doubts: Unresolved conflict rather than a verified doubt. A search summary attributes to Sidiropoulos's 2013 work the sentence that even for k = 2 'the problem remains open' after Lee–Poore. I could not find that sentence in the arXiv version of Sidiropoulos's paper, which I opened and which does not mention Lee–Poore, and the FOCS 2013 PDF returned HTTP 401.
events.direction: Affirmative for the k = 2 reduction piece, if the abstract is right. Disputed.

events.what_happened: Nikhil Kumar, 'An Approximate Generalization of the Okamura–Seymour Theorem', arXiv 2208.00795, v1 1 Aug 2022, v2 29 Oct 2022, v3 10 Jan 2025; a FOCS 2022 version and a SIAM DOI 10.1137/23M1545938 appear in search results. The abstract, which I opened, gives an ℓ1 embedding of a planar metric that approximately preserves distances between all pairs of points on the same face, with an approximate max-flow min-cut consequence for same-face demands. No constant is stated in the abstract.
events.delivers: Planar metrics, for pairs of points on the same face only. A restricted setting, and the abstract does not give a constant.
events.remains: Pairs not on a common face, which is the general planar case.

disputes.summary: Lee and Poore (SoCG 2013) claim the 2-sum embedding conjecture for every finite family F (abstract on Lee's publication page, opened). A search-result summary attributes to Sidiropoulos's 2013 work the sentence that even for k = 2 the problem remains open. I could not find that sentence in the arXiv version of Sidiropoulos (opened; it does not mention Lee–Poore), and the FOCS 2013 PDF returned HTTP 401. Unresolved.

The reader's blog says the minor-free case would follow from the planar and bounded-treewidth results by the Robertson–Seymour decomposition. Search summaries of Lee and Sidiropoulos (STOC 2009; full text not opened) say the general conjecture reduces to the planar conjecture plus a k-sum embedding conjecture. The blog's sketch does not mention a k-sum step. Unresolved, and it decides whether the 2026 claims would reach the general problem.

The OpenAI repository claims the planar case, which conflicts with the status 'open' given by the Wikipedia article (last edited 27 Dec 2025, cached copy), Sidiropoulos 2013, Kumar 2022 and the 7 Oct 2026 k-outerplanar paper. The last of these was most likely written before the 6 Oct release. No named expert has confirmed or refuted the OpenAI claim.

summary: Thirty-five web searches and about forty page fetches turned up no human-verified resolution of the GNRS conjecture as of 11 October 2026. The Wikipedia article (cached copy, last edited 27 December 2025) lists no developments after 2013. The development that bears directly on the problem is an OpenAI repository, openai/math, whose first public commit is dated 6 October 2026 ('Initial commit' on the commit page; a later commit on 8 October updated manuscripts and Lean formalizations). It contains two manuscripts that bear on this problem: one claiming a single constant for ℓ1 distortion of all planar graphs, and one claiming a constant C(k) for graphs of bounded treewidth. The README attributes the batch to 'an unreleased internal OpenAI model' and gives the batch as 719 manuscripts in 372 families (aggregator reports say 722; I used the README). I could not extract either PDF's text, so my knowledge of the content comes from the Lean statements (PlanarL1.lean and BoundedTreewidthL1.lean, fetched on 11 October) and the Lean docs file. In both copies read, the main theorem is proved by sorry; the files state the claims but do not prove them. A third-party catalogue (sites.pitt.edu, not opened because it exceeded the fetch size limit) describes both as resolving their cases positively. A reader's blog (Hung Le, 7 to 11 October; read through a summarising fetch) describes partial reading, calls parts of the argument hard to follow, and says the minor-free case is not among OpenAI's solutions. The planar claim, if correct, settles the planar family; the treewidth claim, if correct, gives per-k constants for bounded-treewidth families. Both are new cases on the sources' account: bounded-treewidth families contain all trees, so the 2009 Lee–Sidiropoulos result for families that do not contain all trees does not reach them, and treewidth 2 was already known (Chakrabarti et al. 2008). Neither claim, taken alone, settles the general conjecture, because the Lee–Sidiropoulos reduction (as cited in search summaries) also needs a k-sum statement, and the k = 2 case of that statement is disputed. The repository's own README says that the attribution covers 'the vast majority' of results, that the planar and treewidth manuscripts are not among its two named exceptions, and that some unformalized results 'could have issues'. The planar and treewidth manuscripts have no named human author in what I could read, and I found no arXiv, journal or referee record for them. A second 2026 item, Chang, Conroy, Eliot, Le and Vinayak (arXiv 2610.10888, 7 Oct 2026), improves the k-dependence for k-outerplanar graphs from 2^O(k) to poly(k); that family was already settled in 2003, so this is a bound moving for a settled family, not a resolution. Discarded items, each recorded with its reason: Kalantarzadeh and Kumar (2025), a lower bound on the planar multiflow–multicut gap, a related but different quantity; Chekuri and Jain (2026), directed planar graphs; Duan (2026), a namesake, the GNS conjecture of Gabrielov, Novikov and Shapiro; Filtser (2024), an ℓ∞ result; and Chang et al. (2024), a stochastic embedding into bounded-treewidth hosts. Three OpenAI manuscripts were withdrawn one day after release for a sign error, and fourteen were revised; per secondary summaries (not opened) none of the withdrawn items concerns ℓ1 embeddings. On AI: the authors of the planar and treewidth manuscripts are not named, and the one system credited is the repository's 'unreleased internal OpenAI model', recorded as the repository's statement rather than the manuscript's, since I could not read the manuscript. The reader used a ChatGPT-family assistant to work through the manuscript; that is a reader's aid, not an author credit, and I have not recorded it as a system. The OpenAI 'Ten advances' batch of 1 August 2026, checked through the ten-proofs Lean repository, contains nothing on ℓ1 embeddings.
competing_reading: The strongest case for taking the 6 October 2026 manuscripts seriously: they are the first claims to settle the planar family and bounded-treewidth families outright, they come with formal statements, and the one qualified reader found the early lemmas straightforward and the method new rather than wrong. If the same method handles k-sums, the full GNRS conjecture would follow, which the reader's blog predicts. On that reading the event is a resolution of the conjecture's planar and treewidth cases with a plausible path to the general case. The contrary case: the Lean main theorems are proved by sorry in the copies read, the qualified reader reports that parts of the argument are incomplete or unclear, no named human has verified the work, and it arrived in a batch in which other manuscripts were withdrawn within a day. On that reading the event is an unverified partial claim, and the general case is not shown to follow.
what_would_settle_it: (a) A sorry-free Lean proof of planar_graph_metrics_embed_L1 and main_theorem (BoundedTreewidthL1.lean), checked by someone other than the authors, or a reported build of the current files with a sorry count. (b) A public verification, refereed publication, or explicit error report from a named ℓ1-embedding specialist (for example Filtser, Lee, Sidiropoulos, Naor or Rabinovich). (c) A statement from OpenAI or the repository identifying the exact model and prompt chain for each of these two manuscripts, and whether any human wrote part of the argument. (d) The k-sum step: a proof, or a published reduction, from the planar and bounded-treewidth results to all proper minor-closed families. (e) The full text of Lee and Poore (SoCG 2013) and of the FOCS 2013 version of Sidiropoulos, to settle the k = 2 dispute. (f) Opening the Pitt-hosted catalogue and the Nature report, which I could not open, to compare their descriptions with the repository.

incomplete: (1) The planar and treewidth manuscripts' PDFs could not be read by my tools, so their content, authorship, acknowledgements and proofs are not recorded from the papers themselves. Their statements come from the Lean files and the Lean docs (fetched through a summarising tool, with the sorry lines confirmed by a second fetch for the planar file), the README, and the reader's blog. (2) The README and the blog were read through a summarising fetch. Quoted sentences are as the tool returned them and were not checked character-for-character against the page. (3) The Pitt-hosted catalogue exceeded the fetch size limit and was not opened. The Nature report and the Retraction Watch report were not reached; withdrawal and batch-count details come from aggregators and are flagged as such. (4) Several pre-window sources are cited from secondary snippets and not opened: Gupta et al. (1999 and 2004), Chekuri et al. (2003), Rao (1999), Chakrabarti et al. (2008), Lee and Raghavendra (2010), Krauthgamer, Lee and Rika (2018/2019), the Lee–Sidiropoulos STOC 2009 full text (including its planar and k-sum reduction), the Lee–Poore full text, and the FOCS 2013 Sidiropoulos PDF (HTTP 401). The dispute about k = 2 therefore remains open. (5) Full text was not read for the 2026 k-outerplanar paper (2610.10888), the 2024 treewidth-host paper (2411.00216), or the other arXiv items; the AI disclosure for those rests on their abstract pages. (6) No Google Scholar, MathSciNet, zbMATH 'cited by', Quanta, Tao's blog or Lean Zulip check was possible; later citations of the 2026 OpenAI manuscripts beyond the blog and the aggregator reports were not established. (7) The Lean files were not built locally. (8) The Wikipedia article was read as a cached copy and may lag current edits.
